meta.subject: English
meta.topic: Activity 2 of 9 (quiz/game): Guided Fill-In - Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions
meta.title: Pause Points: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that creates a dramatic pause before an emphatic final word: The judges' decision was___
questions.explanation: The dash creates a dramatic pause and sets off the final word for emphasis.
questions.skill: Using a dash for emphasis
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation needed before for when it joins two independent clauses: The practice was canceled___ several players were injured.
questions.explanation: A comma precedes for when it joins two independent clauses, as it does here.
questions.skill: Using a comma before for between independent clauses
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the standard punctuation before the coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses: The survey results were surprising___ the researchers began checking them again.
questions.explanation: A comma separates the two independent clauses before the coordinating conjunction and.
questions.skill: Punctuating independent clauses joined by and
questions.topic: Guided Fill-In - Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that signals one or more actions have been omitted from the sequence: The hikers checked the map, shared supplies___ and continued north.
questions.explanation: The ellipsis indicates that one or more actions are omitted between the actions named before and after it.
questions.skill: Using ellipses for omitted words
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that shows the list continues beyond the examples given: The archive contained letters, photographs, maps___
questions.explanation: An ellipsis at the end of the list indicates that more examples continue beyond those named.
questions.skill: Showing omitted list items with an ellipsis
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that shows words are omitted at the beginning of the sentence: ___the judges had reached a decision.
questions.explanation: The ellipsis at the beginning signals that the opening words of the sentence have been left out.
questions.skill: Initial ellipsis for omitted words
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation required after the introductory prepositional phrase: Beneath the old oak, ___ a family of wrens had built a nest.
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory prepositional phrase Beneath the old oak and marks the pause before the main clause.
questions.skill: Using commas after introductory phrases
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that separates the nonrestrictive appositive from the rest of the sentence: A retired engineer, Dr. Patel___ reviewed the plans.
questions.explanation: The comma separates the nonrestrictive appositive Dr. Patel from the rest of the sentence.
questions.skill: Using commas with nonrestrictive appositives
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the standard list punctuation that separates the items while leaving the repeated verb understood before each one: We packed bread___ and cheese.
questions.explanation: The commas separate the list items and make it clear that packed is understood before each item.
questions.skill: Using commas in lists with omitted words
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that marks a brief pause between two closely connected independent clauses, without signaling the stronger division of a semicolon or the dramatic break of a dash: The bell rang___ everyone rushed to class.
questions.explanation: The comma marks the brief pause after the bell rang and keeps the closely related actions in one sentence.
questions.skill: Using commas between independent clauses
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that separates a final direct address from the rest of the sentence: We should leave now___ everyone.
questions.explanation: A comma separates a final vocative such as everyone from the sentence's main clause.
questions.skill: Punctuating a final vocative
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that separates coordinate adjectives before a noun: The hiker faced a long___ difficult trail.
questions.explanation: A comma separates coordinate adjectives that equally modify the noun.
questions.skill: Identify comma for coordinate adjectives
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that suggests a sound gradually fading into the distance: The singer's final note echoed___
questions.explanation: An ellipsis can suggest that a sound is fading away or trailing off.
questions.skill: Using an ellipsis to suggest fading sound
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that shows a brief hesitation before the speaker continues with a complete thought: The cause of the delay was... a network failure.
questions.explanation: The ellipsis marks a hesitation before the speaker supplies the completed explanation.
questions.skill: Using an ellipsis to show hesitation
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the pair of dashes that sets off a parenthetical phrase in the middle of the sentence: The experiment___though expensive___finally produced a clear result.
choices: : though expensive: finally produced a clear result.
, though expensive, finally produced a clear result.
; though expensive; finally produced a clear result.
questions.explanation: The pair of dashes sets off the parenthetical phrase “though expensive” without confusing the main elements of the sentence.
questions.skill: Using paired dashes to set off parenthetical information
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that shows an abrupt interruption within a sentence: The climber called for help___ the rope shifted sharply.
questions.explanation: The em dash marks the abrupt interruption between the climber's call for help and the rope's sudden movement.
questions.skill: Using dashes for abrupt breaks
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation needed because the relative clause identifies which singer won: The singer ___ who performed at the benefit concert won first prize.
choices: , who performed at the benefit concert,
who performed at the benefit concert,
who performed at the benefit concert
: who performed at the benefit concert
questions.explanation: Because the clause identifies which singer won, it is restrictive and should not be separated from the subject by commas.
questions.skill: Distinguishing restrictive from nonrestrictive clauses
questions.topic: Guided Fill-In - Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the punctuation that sets off a brief explanation while keeping the sentence grammatical: The trail was flooded___we found a higher path___ and continued.
questions.explanation: The paired dashes set off the explanation as an interruption while keeping the sentence from becoming a comma splice.
questions.skill: Using paired dashes for an explanatory interruption
questions.topic: Guided Fill-In: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the standard punctuation that separates the nonrestrictive phrase from the rest of the sentence: The backpack___with its straps already buckled, hung by the door.
questions.explanation: A comma sets off the nonrestrictive phrase with its straps already buckled from the main clause.
questions.skill: Comma before a nonrestrictive prepositional phrase
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that shows an unstated phrase has been omitted from the middle of a quotation: 'Before leaving, he whispered, Wait for the signal___then cross safely.'
questions.explanation: The ellipsis marks the unstated words between Wait for the signal and then cross safely.
questions.skill: Ellipsis for omitted words within a quotation
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the standard punctuation after the introductory dependent clause: After the rehearsal ended___ the cast gathered for notes.
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory dependent clause After the rehearsal ended.
questions.skill: Using a comma after an introductory dependent clause
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that correctly separates the introductory participial phrase from the main clause: Reviewing the data carefully, ___
choices: : the researcher found a clear pattern.
— the researcher found a clear pattern.
... the researcher found a clear pattern.
, the researcher found a clear pattern.
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory participial phrase Reviewing the data carefully and separates it from the main clause.
questions.skill: Comma after an introductory participial phrase
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that creates a strong break before the explanation while keeping the sentence continuous: The coach rewrote the playbook___ it was missing a crucial safety step.
questions.explanation: The dash creates a strong break within the sentence and signals that the following clause explains why the playbook was rewritten.
questions.skill: Using dashes to create strong breaks
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the paired em dashes that set off an explanatory phrase while allowing a comma within it: The principal announced the schedule___classes would begin at eight, buses at seven___before the crowd dispersed.
choices: : classes would begin at eight, buses at seven:
, classes would begin at eight, buses at seven,
... classes would begin at eight, buses at seven ...
—classes would begin at eight, buses at seven—
questions.explanation: The paired em dashes set off the complete parenthetical explanation and allow the comma to separate the two parts of the aside.
questions.skill: Paired dashes around a parenthetical explanation
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that shows words have been omitted at the end of a quoted sentence: The letter read, 'I will always remember you___'
questions.explanation: An ellipsis at the end of a quotation indicates omitted trailing words.
questions.skill: Identify ellipsis for omission at end of quotation
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that correctly separates an introductory dependent clause from the main clause: Although the trail was muddy___ the hikers reached the summit before noon.
choices: . The hikers reached the summit before noon.
; the hikers reached the summit before noon.
: the hikers reached the summit before noon.
, the hikers reached the summit before noon.
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory dependent clause beginning with “Although.”
questions.skill: Using a comma after an introductory dependent clause
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that shows the final ingredient has been left out: The recipe called for flour, sugar, and ___
questions.explanation: The ellipsis indicates that the list of ingredients is deliberately left unfinished.
questions.skill: Using ellipses for omission
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that closes the nonrestrictive appositive: My sister, a skilled violinist___ performed at the recital.
questions.explanation: A comma closes the nonrestrictive appositive phrase.
questions.skill: Identify comma for nonrestrictive appositive
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the dash that creates a strong break before an explanatory dependent clause: The road ended at the cliff___ where the land dropped far below.
choices: ... where the land dropped far below.
, where the land dropped far below.
; where the land dropped far below.
— where the land dropped far below.
questions.explanation: The em dash introduces the dependent clause with a strong break and emphasizes the explanation about the land.
questions.skill: Using a dash before an explanatory clause
questions.topic: Guided Fill-In - Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correctly punctuated ending of the speaker's unfinished remark: The speaker trailed off, saying, 'The meeting is over___
questions.explanation: The ellipsis shows that the speaker's words trail off rather than ending with a complete thought.
questions.skill: Using ellipses for trailing off
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that creates a strong break before the unexpected result: The battery was nearly full___ the device shut down anyway.
questions.explanation: An em dash creates the strong break before the unexpected result.
questions.skill: Using an em dash to emphasize an unexpected result
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that sets off a nonrestrictive clause in the middle of a sentence: The museum, which opened last year___ attracts thousands of visitors.
questions.explanation: A comma closes the nonrestrictive clause before the main verb.
questions.skill: Identify comma for nonrestrictive clause
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the standard punctuation after an introductory infinitive phrase: To reach the train on time___ we left the house an hour early.
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory infinitive phrase before the main clause begins.
questions.skill: Punctuating an introductory infinitive phrase
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation required between the two independent clauses in a not only...but also construction: Maya not only found the missing file in the shared drive after the server came back online___ but she also corrected it.
questions.explanation: The comma separates the two independent clauses and marks the second part of the not only...but also construction.
questions.skill: Using a comma in a not only...but also construction
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that shows the speaker leaves the thought unfinished: The announcer began, 'The guest speaker is___'
questions.explanation: An ellipsis signals that the speaker's thought is deliberately left unfinished.
questions.skill: Showing an unfinished thought with an ellipsis
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the paired dashes that set off a brief, strongly emphasized correction inside the sentence: The test was difficult___not impossible___and everyone finished it.
questions.explanation: Paired dashes set off the correction and give it stronger emphasis than ordinary commas would.
questions.skill: Using paired dashes for an emphasized correction
questions.topic: Guided Fill-In - Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that shows words omitted at the end of a quotation: The narrator said, 'We reached the island___
choices: ... but no boat was in sight.
— but no boat was in sight.
; but no boat was in sight.
, but no boat was in sight.
questions.explanation: The ellipsis shows that the quotation trails off with words left unstated.
questions.skill: Using an ellipsis for an unfinished quotation
questions.topic: Guided Fill-In - Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that marks words left unstated in the middle of a sentence: She had prepared the speech, checked the slides, and rehearsed the introduction... the final question caught her off guard.
choices: : the final question caught her off guard.
— the final question caught her off guard.
, the final question caught her off guard.
... the final question caught her off guard.
questions.explanation: The ellipsis signals that the linking words between the preparations and the final event have been left unstated.
questions.skill: Using an ellipsis for an omitted transition
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the standard punctuation after an introductory interjection: Well___ I had not expected that turn of events.
questions.explanation: A comma conventionally separates an introductory interjection such as Well from the rest of the sentence.
questions.skill: Punctuating an introductory interjection
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the dash that creates a strong break before the explanation: Her explanation was brief but complete___the delay had been caused by a broken sensor.
choices: — the delay had been caused by a broken sensor.
, the delay had been caused by a broken sensor.
... the delay had been caused by a broken sensor.
: the delay had been caused by a broken sensor.
questions.explanation: The em dash creates a strong break before the explanation without creating a comma splice between the two independent clauses.
questions.skill: Dash before an explanatory clause
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation needed to set off a nonrestrictive appositive: The coach, a former Olympic sprinter, ___ encouraged us after every setback.
questions.explanation: The comma closes the pair of commas that sets off the appositive, which adds information about the coach.
questions.skill: Setting off a nonrestrictive appositive
questions.topic: Guided Fill-In - Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that suggests an action continued beyond the repeated words: The team practiced, practiced, and___
questions.explanation: The ellipsis after the repeated and suggests that the team continued practicing.
questions.skill: Using an ellipsis for continuation
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the dash that marks an abrupt shift in the action while keeping the two parts closely connected: The runner reached the line—___ then collapsed.
questions.explanation: The dash creates a strong break before the sudden action and gives the second part added emphasis.
questions.skill: Using a dash for an abrupt action shift
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that marks a brief pause after a direct name before making a request: Lina, ___ could you pass the salt?
questions.explanation: A comma follows a direct name used to address someone and marks the brief pause before the request.
questions.skill: Using a comma after direct address
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that separates the introductory absolute phrase from the main clause: His hands trembling,___ the speaker began his testimony.
questions.explanation: The comma sets off the introductory absolute phrase His hands trembling from the main clause.
questions.skill: Setting off introductory absolute phrases
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the dash that creates a strong break between two complete statements: The final bell rang___ we tore out of the classroom.
choices: — we tore out of the classroom.
; we tore out of the classroom.
: we tore out of the classroom.
, we tore out of the classroom.
questions.explanation: The dash creates a strong break between the two complete statements and emphasizes the sudden rush to leave.
questions.skill: Using a dash to create a strong break between statements
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that shows words omitted from the beginning of the quotation: '___ and then the lights went out.'
choices: : and then the lights went out.
, and then the lights went out.
; and then the lights went out.
... and then the lights went out.
questions.explanation: The opening ellipsis shows that the quotation begins in the middle of the original words.
questions.skill: Using an ellipsis to show omitted words at the beginning
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that conventionally follows the greeting in a formal letter: Dear Ms. Alvarez___ thank you for sending the revised proposal.
choices: , thank you for sending the revised proposal.
; thank you for sending the revised proposal.
: thank you for sending the revised proposal.
. Thank you for sending the revised proposal.
questions.explanation: A comma follows the salutation “Dear Ms. Alvarez” before the body of the letter begins.
questions.skill: Using a comma after a formal salutation
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with punctuation that marks a final afterthought: The class ended early. We can discuss the essay___
questions.explanation: The dash marks tomorrow as a final afterthought while keeping it closely connected to the preceding statement.
questions.skill: Using dashes for afterthoughts
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the punctuation that marks the pause after the introductory phrase: The hikers, tired but determined, ___ continued onward.
questions.explanation: The comma closes the introductory phrase and separates it from the main clause.
questions.skill: Using commas after introductory phrases
questions.topic: Ellipses, Dashes, and Commas for Pauses and Omissions

feedback.lose: The draw piled up this time. Review the pause marks and try again.
